start_here: You never call it yourself. Say to your AI: "List my files"; tool:your-files asks tool:your-files-names for the names through its own door, and the engine starts the names session on the first call.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps the names of your files as rows in your own database.
instructions: 1. Make sure your database connection (own-rows-postgres-connection) is saved in your vault; the engine mounts it on descriptor 3 of this run alone and never prints it.

2. Use your files through tool:your-files. Each names read or change it makes is one call of this tool: tools:run with {tool: "tool:your-files-names", call: {name, arguments}}, where name is one operation of the store's rows (get, get_many, held_record_with_version, list_page, ids, mutate, stamp, totals, search, place, order, changes, minted, wait_for_order).
3. Each answer comes back as a file of bytes (the row's session.byte_result), so a page of rows is never cut to fit one message.

worked_examples.title: Where my files' names are kept
worked_examples.ask: Where are the names of my files kept?
worked_examples.hands_back: {tool: "tool:your-files-names", result: {structuredContent: {bytes: {file, total, offset, length}}}}: the bytes of {answer: "postgres://<host>:<port>/<name>"}.
